Anchor.description:
Where a comment was left: the app page, the place on it, what was there
in words, and the ticket the element belongs to (when it belongs to one).

`route`, `path` and `label` are required and not blank; `excerpt` may be
empty (an element with no text). Each is trimmed. They are `#[serde(default)]`
so that one left out arrives as empty and is refused *in band*, naming
it — not as a transport error before the method runs.

excerpt.description: What was there, in words: its text, e.g. `DEMAND-1` (may be empty).

label.description: What was there, in words: the element's name, e.g. `Parent chip`.

path.description:
Where on the page: the element's path, e.g.
`[data-tag="ticket DEMAND-1"]`. `list { path }` matches a prefix of it.

route.description:
The app page, as its route: `#/ticket/DEMAND-2`, `#/waves/RETURNS`,
`#/` (the board) — always beginning `#/`.

ticket.description:
The ticket the element belongs to, e.g. `DEMAND-2` — omitted when it
belongs to none. It must name a ticket; kept as that ticket's id.

version.description:
Set by the server, never by the caller: `ticket`'s `updated_unix`
when the comment was added — so a reader can tell the ticket has
changed since (its body may no longer hold `path`). Omitted with no
`ticket`; a value sent is replaced.

AnswerSource.description:
INPUT-3: who made a change to an input (INPUT-1's language) — `app`, a
viewer's click, which the host says on its `answer`; `api`, everything
else (synapse, an agent). The only "who" until CONTEXT adds identity.

oneOf.description:
MENGER-13: the store itself — an input withdrawn because its ticket
was canceled, or restored when it was not any more. Never a caller's
to say: `inputs.answer` and `inputs.clear` refuse it.

at.description: When it was added, unix seconds.

author.description:
Who left it: its name (ACCESS-19: signed by the caller — its
principal when it has no name; `owner` on one kept before ACCESS-24,
when login could be off).

id.description: Its id: 1, 2, … in the order comments were added, never reused.

intent.description: APP-23: `changes` for a change request; omitted for a comment.

principal.description:
IDENTITY-21: the Plexus principal of who left it, when they were
signed in — `author` is only the name they go by.

reply_to.description:
COMMENT-8: the comment this answers — always a thread's root (a
reply to a reply is a reply to its root); omitted for a root.

CommentId.description: COMMENT-2: a comment's number, from 1 in the order kept.

CommentIntent.description: What a comment is: a comment, or a change request (any case)

Ending.description: APP-24: how a ticket ended for an agent waiting on it.

InputValue.description:
INPUT-3: an answer's value, typed by its input's kind — internally
tagged, as [`Placement`] is: `{"type": "choice", "option": "archive"}`
(one option's `value`), `{"type": "multi", "options": ["a", "b"]}` (a set
of them — stored in the order the body declares them, each once; it may
be empty: none ticked), `{"type": "text", "text": "…"}` (a reply, not
blank). Through synapse, a param's fields are dotted flags:
`--value.type choice --value.option archive`.

QueueAction.description: What one queue write did — a [`QueueRecord`]'s action.

oneOf.description: Queued again, at a higher urgency.

Queued again at the same urgency or a lower one: the urgency kept,
the reason (and input) the new ones.
Taken out — the owner done with it, or the caller withdrawing it.
Taken out because its named input was closed.

APP-23: handed back — the owner requested changes (the record names
the comment that says which).

ARCHIVE-2: taken out because the ticket was archived — an archived
ticket asks nothing.

Reply.description:
APP-24: what answered an agent waiting on a ticket (`tickets.await_reply`)
— the first response on it since the call's `since`.

oneOf.description:
An input on the ticket was answered (with `input` named: that one):
the value, the rationale, from where (`app` — a reader's click — or
`api`), when.

APP-23: the owner requested changes — the comment that says which
(intent `changes`); the ticket is out of the queue.
Someone other than the caller commented on the ticket.

Someone other than the caller took the ticket out of the queue
(`action`: `unqueued`, or `closed` — its named input was closed).
The ticket was canceled or deleted (`how`): nothing more will come.

ARCHIVE-2: the ticket was archived (by `by`, itself or with an
ancestor): it asks nothing any more.
